content.thinking:
I'm planning the design for an Overwatch-style chopper motorbike: dark gunmetal body with white panels and an orange accent, roughly 2.4 meters long and about 1.1-1.25 meters tall with ape-hanger handlebars, modeled facing +Z with proportional wheel sizes.

Now I'm working out wheel geometry using torus shapes rotated to align their axis with X for the tires, scaling them wider for the fat rear tire, and planning cylinder rims with solid Overwatch-style hub details instead of traditional spokes.

For spokes and brake discs I'm using thin radial rods plus small cylinders in the YZ plane, then defining axle and steering head coordinates (rear axle, front axle, steering head position) to lay out the fork geometry connecting frame tubes.

I'm cranking the fork rake to an extreme ~47° for a chopper look, positioning the steering head high and forward while pulling the front axle further out. From there I'm routing the main frame: a top tube from the head back to a seat post, hardtail rails down to the rear axle, plus placing the V-twin engine block and tank along the top tube.

For the tank I'm shaping it as a scaled sphere to get a teardrop profile, then painting it with a simple stripe pattern -- a white center band over an orange body with darker shading underneath -- using a coordinate-based paint function rather than a texture decal. I'm now planning out the overall parts list, aiming for roughly 150 components total.

I'm setting up a limited color palette (gunmetal, steel, chrome, white, orange accent, black, rubber, leather) and defining warm glow colors for the headlight and taillight, then starting to build out the part list with mirrored wheels and swept frame tubes.

Still plotting frame geometry...

Still working out fork geometry...

Now I'm positioning the headlight forward of the fork, around (0,1.0,0.55), using a cylinder oriented along the z-axis to form the lens and housing with a chrome ring and glowing disc face.

Checking placement, I realize it overlaps the head tube collider — I'll push the headlight further forward to z=0.62 with small bracket rods connecting it to the fork legs so it reads as mounted properly. Next I'm sketching the front fender as a curved sweep arc over the wheel, defining control points for a catmull spline following the tire radius.

Working out the rotation order to position the arc toward the top-front of the wheel...

Now I'm sizing the rear fender torus with a bobbed arc over the rear tire, checking clearances against the tire's outer radius, and planning the V-twin engine layout with an angled crankcase box and tilted front cylinder.

Still planning engine geometry...

I'll place torus discs along tangent directions for the heat shield bands, tapering pipe radius slightly over the path, then work out the chain guard and rear sprocket placement relative to the rail and tire widths so the rails sit properly inside the tire footprint.

Adding the belt tangent rods, a rear brake disc with orange caliper, and checking front fork clearance to fit a front brake disc without hitting the tire.

Now I'm working out floor contact heights from torus radii on both wheels, then setting up the solo seat shape using a lofted outline across multiple stations.

For the tank, I'm adding a chrome filler cap, mounting rods, and a stylized chevron/hex decal on both sides instead of logos, using a hard-edged two-tone paint split (white top, orange flash, gunmetal underside based on normal direction) for that bold color-blocking look. Then I'm placing a gunmetal oil tank/battery box under the seat.

Now I'm working out forward foot controls—pegs mounted on rods extending from the engine area with rubber grips—plus a kickstand built as an angled rod running from the frame down to a foot that touches the floor.

I'm also sketching the taillight placement and figuring out the rear fender's curvature and endpoint so the overall wheelbase lands near the typical chopper length of about 2.4 units.

I'll skip the sissy bar and saddle bags, but add a thin black brake line sweeping from the handlebar to the front caliper and cable lines for detail.

For the headlight area, I'm adding small orange glow spheres as turn signals at the handlebar ends instead of the fork. For the underglow, I'm settling on simple glow rings as orange discs in the wheel hub centers rather than floating rods beneath the engine or pinstripes on the rocker covers.

Now I'm placing an orange air cleaner cylinder with a chrome ring torus and disc on the engine's right side, and planning a decal texture for the tank with a white swoosh, dark stripe, and hexagon graphic to apply via the decal system.

I'm working out the decal orientation math for the tank's +X side — figuring out which direction is "right" relative to the viewer looking down -X with Y as up, so the graphic faces correctly without mirroring issues.

Rather than solving the full directionality problem, I decide to design the decal symmetrically with a slanted band and stripes so direction doesn't matter. Then I move to the wheel tread, planning to paint tire blocks onto the torus geometry using UV coordinates — mapping around the major circle and across the tube cross-section.

Working out tread, sidewall, and shoulder regions from the torus v-coordinate...

Now I'm figuring out the wheel rim geometry, planning to build it as two disc faces plus a cylindrical hub for the sides.

Working through the geometry, the tire opening is only visible around radius 0.16-0.17, so I'll set the hub face as a cylinder of radius 0.18 and height 0.14 spanning that gap, with a thin orange accent torus added on the face for visual detail.

For the front wheel, I'll use a slightly larger torus radius with matching rim cylinder and hub discs, then build a reusable wheel function that assembles the tire torus, rim cylinder, and face discs together with configurable radius, tube size, and spoke parameters.

Adding wheel face details and spokes...

Now I'm working out the engine block: a crankcase box with side covers, a gearbox housing behind it, and two angled cylinder barrels splayed forward and rear in a V configuration.

Still placing pushrods and intake tubing...

I need to resolve the spatial conflicts between the exhaust pipes, drive rails, and pulley near the rear wheel—shifting pipes out to x=±0.3 to clear the tire and sprocket area, while keeping rails at ±0.19 and figuring out where the pulley disc fits without overlapping everything.

Placing bracket positions...

I'm angling the down tube from the frame cradle to the mounting point, skipping the engine mount plates since they're hidden, and now routing the brake hose as a curved path from the handlebar grip down to the front caliper on the fork leg.

Deciding to skip mirrors since ape-hanger bars already push the height near 1.45, opting instead for bar-end blinker spheres, then working out the handlebar riser position from the top triple tree clamp and the curved path the bars take upward and outward.

Now I'm figuring out where the grip rods and brake levers attach at the bar ends, sizing them small with chrome and black materials, then placing the gauge cluster housing on the triple tree with a cylindrical lens and a textured circular face angled to point toward the rider.

For the gauge face I'm designing a dark-dial SVG texture with an orange arc, tick marks, and a white needle. I'm also figuring out the side cover panels—extruding teardrop-shaped outlines on each side of the frame with bevels and orange coloring, and positioning a decal graphic onto their outer faces so it reads correctly given the panel's thickness and orientation.

Now I'm reconciling frame placement: the rails overlap the side covers slightly, which I'm letting pass since the pieces will just merge visually. I'm also sketching the battery box dimensions behind the covers, then working out the seat loft stations and tank scale/position so the tank back and seat front overlap sensibly in height and depth.

I'm checking that the top tube passes beneath the tank without clashing, since the tube's y-position at each z-point stays hidden inside or under the tank. For the seat I'm adding chrome spring posts as mounting rods, skipping a sissy bar, and confirming this is a hardtail so no rear shock is needed—just a seat strut. Now I'm starting on the rear fender struts, running rods from the rear axle position.

Still defining fender geometry...

Verifying the rotation math: confirming local x maps to world -z and local z to world +x, consistent with my earlier assumption.

Checking the torus arc axis alignment, the wheel tire ring orientation, and the cylinder rotation mapping y to -x, all of which check out correctly. I'm also confirming the fork stanchion offset uses a fixed x value along U, and verifying the head tube rod geometry and rake angle details.

Now I'm defining the fork components: the gun-colored tube with orange rings, triple tree rods in chrome, gaiter covers in black, stanchion boots, and lower legs in white with axle lugs. I'm settling on gun-colored frame with orange accents and starting to think through panel line details like the tank cap.

Still placing details...

I'll skip the belt guard for now and focus on positioning the engine within x range ±0.15, placing the belt at 0.235 with the front sprocket near x=.21 and gearbox around x ±0.12, plus adding an engine side cover disc near x=0.155.

I'm checking for geometric conflicts between the sprocket and gearbox placements across their x/z ranges, which seem fine, then estimating total part count across wheels, forks, and other components at roughly 200. I'm deciding to skip a toon/cel shading kit to reduce risk, and settling on which modules to import from the builder and path utilities.

I'm reviewing other samples to confirm the correct import pattern for createBuilder and the expected default export structure, and nailing down the exact meta object format with name, description, style, and commit fields. I'm also working through the type signatures for the sweep, rod, and part builder methods, covering how radius tapering and scale/fill options are typed.

Now I'm checking the paint function's unused parameter naming convention, the decal method's surface target typing, and how to compute tangent and radius values along a catmull path for the tail pipe bands, plus setting up the fin discs using cylinder parts with directional vectors.

Still writing cylinder parts...

Still writing SVG graphics...

Still writing tire paint logic...

Baking the paint into the texture via UV so it stays efficient, and parts can reference glow effects through b.part with strength values, keeping palette count under 64. I'm also checking the overall dimension, with z spanning roughly -1.28 to 1.

Now I'm defining the forks using a normalized direction vector and axis offsets, plus setting up the headlight geometry: a scaled sphere for the housing, a torus ring, and a glowing lens disc, with supporting bracket rods positioned around the frame.

I'm also placing a small glowing taillight box near the rear fender, computing its position from the fender's angle and offset, with a red-orange glow color.

Placing the taillight box near the tube end so it overlaps slightly, and orienting the plate so it faces backward correctly when viewed from behind. Now I need to figure out the fender thickness scaling...

For colors, I'm deciding to keep the tank white-topped, fenders mostly white with the rear one orange, frame and engine gunmetal with chrome accents. For the kickstand, I'm positioning the rod on the right side to avoid the pulley, running from near the frame down to a ground pad, with a small box as the foot pad.

Checking ground clearance, I confirm tires sit at y=0 and the kickstand pad floats just slightly above it, which is fine. Now I'm working out brake discs and calipers for front and rear wheels — placing thin steel cylinder discs near the fork and swingarm, with small orange caliper boxes aligned to the fork's tilt direction. I'm also positioning the rear pulley as a cylinder, checking it clears the rail supports at x=±0.19 without overlapping, and sizing the rear wheel hub and rim dimensions for the wheel face geometry.

Working through the tire and rim geometry math for both wheels, I'm calculating where the face discs and decorative spokes should sit relative to the tire's torus profile so they appear to bulge slightly beyond the tire opening rather than floating inside it — adjusting rim half-width and disc radius values for front and rear to get a visually convincing wheel plate.

Now I'm sketching out the spoke geometry (six rods per wheel at 60° intervals, box-section rods colored dark against a white disc), plus a rim-edge torus ring, chrome hub cylinder, and glowing accent disc. I'm also planning the axle rod, small chrome bolt spheres around the hub, and seat details like leather grain texture and stitched edge rods in orange along the seat perimeter.

Working through the seat pan geometry and loft parameters, then double-checking sweep/torus function signatures and texture handling for the gauge face and plate before writing the final file.
